title: The quotient by the I-power torsion submodule has no I-torsion (I finitely generated)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal and $M$ an $R$-module. Put $M[I^\infty]=\{m\in M:\ I^nm=0\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$, a submodule of $M$, and $M'=M/M[I^\infty]$. Then $M'[I]=0$: if $\bar x\in M'$ satisfies $a\bar x=0$ for every $a\in I$, then $\bar x=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion, line 24042), part (1)

proof.text: Write $T=M[I^\infty]$. This is a submodule: $0\in T$; if $I^pm=0$ and $I^qn=0$, then $I^{\max(p,q)}(m+n)=0$; and if $r\in R$, then $I^p(rm)=rI^pm=0$. For $x\in M$ let $\bar x$ be its class in $M/T$. The condition $I\bar x=0$ means precisely that $ax\in T$ for every $a\in I$, since the kernel of $M\to M/T$ is $T$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24042-24063, opening sentence; submodule and quotient details expanded

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set s for I. For each a in s, membership of ax in T gives an exponent n(a) with I^n(a) annihilating ax. Put N = max({n(a) : a in s} union {0}). Since n(a) <= N and powers of ideals decrease, I^N annihilates ax for every generator a. This includes the empty set without a separate case.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24053-24059: finite generators, individual annihilating powers, and the common exponent

proof.text: Let f : R -> M be the linear map r |-> rx. The inverse image under f of the I^N-torsion submodule contains every generator, hence contains their span I. Thus b(ax)=0 whenever b belongs to I^N and a belongs to I. By I^(N+1)=I^N*I and the ideal multiplication containment criterion, I^(N+1) is contained in ker(f), so I^(N+1)x=0.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24057-24060: the common annihilating power conclusion, with the finite-span and ideal-multiplication argument substituted for monomial expansion

proof.text: The exponent N+1 from step 3 proves x belongs to T by primaryComponent_mem. The quotient kernel criterion therefore gives that its class is zero. If the generating set is empty, N=0 and the same argument uses I^1=0, so no case is omitted.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), lines 24059-24063, conclusion of part (1)
